idiom_name: ES module-scope instance (one evaluation per resolved module)
implementation_notes: The module system is the singleton: a module is evaluated once per resolved URL and its namespace, including top-level bindings, is cached and shared by every importer, so a module-scope const is one instance process-wide and the classic getInstance() guard disappears. Encapsulation comes from not exporting the state at all (export accessor functions) or from freezing what is exported. When a class-shaped API is required, an ES2022 static private field gives the same guarantee in one line. Remember the unit of uniqueness: one per module record, so duplicate package copies, differing query strings, workers and test-runner registries each get their own instance.
pitfalls: Uniqueness is per resolved module URL: a package installed twice, './m.js' versus './m.js?v=2', a bundler duplicating a chunk, or another worker/isolate each produce a separate instance with separate state.
Module state outlives tests: once imported it persists for the whole run (jest.resetModules()/vi.resetModules() only affect later dynamic imports), so tests that mutate it leak into each other.
Exporting a mutable object is shared mutable global state; export accessors or Object.freeze() the exported value to keep writes controlled.
Hot module replacement and dynamic import in dev servers can evaluate the module again, silently creating a second instance.

variants.name: Static private class field with lazy accessor
variants.idiom_name: class with a static #instance field and a static getter
variants.implementation_notes: When the API must be class-shaped (instanceof checks, typed fields, subclass factories), one static private field plus ??= gives the same single-instance guarantee with no module-level side effect: the field is invisible outside the class body and the accessor creates it on first call. ES2022 is the floor, because static class fields, private static fields and the logical assignment operators must all be available; the module form stays shorter when no class shape is needed.
pitfalls: A static field is per class per realm: loading two copies of the module yields two classes and therefore two instances.
??= is not atomic across realms: with worker threads each worker's class copy is a different singleton.
Transpiling to older targets replaces private fields with WeakMap-based helpers, changing performance and debuggability.

JavaScript has no private constructors: the class remains constructible from outside unless the constructor checks a private flag and throws, so the static field hides the instance but does not close the second instance path.
